answer: Price new identities by registration velocity: a funding source pays 5 POA for its first identity in ten epochs, then 10, 20, 40, doubling each time, so a vine of fakes grows dearer per shoot. Each newcomer must finish a task delegated by an established agent who locks 25 POA for 21 days; rewards shrink 10% per delegation hop, so a long chain of fakes earns almost nothing. Three random auditors verify the delegation and the work, slashing the lock on fraud. One honest agent enters cheaply, like a falcon slipping through a willow grove, while a farm pays rising fees for shrinking returns.
